title: Assessing Regional Projections of Marine Climatic Impact‐Drivers Using Coordinated Ensembles: Framework and Application to the Mediterranean Sea
content:
Abstract

The Mediterranean Sea is among the most climate-sensitive regions globally, having experienced unprecedented sea surface temperatures, intensified marine heatwaves, and associated ecosystem impacts in recent years. These changes are projected to intensify throughout the 21st century, with implications for marine ecosystems, biogeochemical processes, and coastal societies. Here, we provide a transferable framework for assessing marine climatic impact-drivers (CIDs) based on key physical ocean essential climate variables, integrating model evaluation, simulation filtering, and confidence assessment of projected changes across global warming levels. The framework is applied to the Mediterranean Sea using a coordinated ensemble of 29 multi-decadal simulations from high-resolution regional climate system models participating in Med-CORDEX. A novel set of marine CIDs is assessed across warming levels from 1.5°C to 4°C, encompassing mean and extreme ocean temperature, mean ocean salinity, vertical stratification, and wind-driven ocean dynamics at basin, sub-basin, and coastal scales. Overall, model responses broadly align with historical trends, increasing confidence in projected changes. Projections indicate robust increases in mean ocean temperature, warm extremes, and stratification across regions as warming intensifies. Under high warming levels, extreme warm events become near-yearly occurrences, whereas cold spells virtually disappear. In contrast, projected changes in salinity, wind stress extremes, and coastal upwelling remain comparatively uncertain across most regions. Beyond the Mediterranean, the proposed framework provides a consistent basis for assessing marine climate risks in other regions as high-resolution regional projections become available, while remaining adaptable to new indicators. To facilitate the exploration of Mediterranean CID projections, an interactive web tool is provided.
